sections.h2: Selling in Biloxi: the water comes first
sections.html:
Biloxi is a Gulf Coast city in Harrison County. The Mississippi Sound forms its southern edge, Biloxi Bay lies to the northeast, and the Back Bay of Biloxi cuts across the middle toward Big Lake. Gulfport borders it to the west and D'Iberville to the north and east. The 2020 count was 49,449 people.

With the elevation at about 20 feet, flood zones come up early in nearly every Biloxi sale. Housing here is a mix of houses that survived Camille in 1969, rebuilds after Katrina came ashore on August 29, 2005 with a surge of about 30 feet, and newer elevated construction. A buyer or inspector will want to know which kind yours is. Keesler Air Force Base sits inside the city, and orders or a job change can set a firm moving date for sellers.

sections.h2: Flood and permit rules before you repair
sections.html:
Building, altering, regrading or filling a Biloxi lot takes a permit from the city's Building Division, and homes in a flood hazard area face stricter standards. The city's flood bulletin says work under $500 carries no permit fee and that new buildings in the floodplain must sit one foot above the base flood elevation.

The rule that surprises sellers is the 50 percent test. When additions, remodeling or repairs to an existing structure add up to 50 percent or more of its market value, the whole building has to meet new-construction standards. A storm-damaged house in a mapped flood zone can cost far more to fix for resale than the visible damage suggests.

  • Call the Community Development Department at (228) 435-6280 before you start repairs on a house in or near a flood zone.
  • Look up the flood map for your address at city offices or any Biloxi library branch, which keep copies of the Flood Insurance Rate Map.
  • Ask whether your planned work would count toward the 50 percent threshold.
  • Hire only a contractor who holds a City of Biloxi license, which the city recommends after storms.

Before work starts, write down what is being repaired, what it costs and who is doing it, and keep the permits and receipts together. A buyer's inspector and a title company both like to see that paper trail, and it helps you prove that repairs stayed under the 50 percent line. If you decide not to repair at all, say so up front and price or sell the house as-is.

Rules change, so confirm current requirements with the city. The city's flood map page explains the map background. Biloxi also runs an environmental court for property maintenance and code cases, so clear any open notice before you list.

Roofs, cooling systems and moisture control dominate repair lists on the coast, because rain and heat come most of the year. Buyers ask about roof age and condition first, and an old air conditioning unit is a real bargaining point.

Standard homeowner's insurance does not pay for flood damage. The city's flood bulletin points owners to a separate National Flood Insurance Program policy. Because Biloxi takes part in the Community Rating System, policyholders get a premium discount. Have your policy and any claim history ready when a buyer asks.

Harrison County mails real property tax bills on December 1 and takes payment without interest until February 1. From February 2 on, interest of one-half of one percent a month applies. Read the county tax collector's page before you list so nothing is delinquent at closing.

Nobody files homestead for you, so check that it is on record. Homestead exemption is not automatic. The assessor's office in Harrison County describes a regular exemption, worth up to $300 in credit on the first $7,500 of assessed value, and a further one for owners who are 65 or older or disabled. On top of that, the state exempts the first $75,000 of true value for a qualifying owner who has reached 65 or is totally disabled.

Think the value is too high? Ask the county Board of Supervisors for a hearing. The usual cutoff is the first Monday in August, ahead of the due date.

sections.h2: What Mississippi requires of a seller
sections.html:
Under Section 89-1-503 of the Mississippi Code, a seller of most homes owes the buyer a signed-off written statement of the property's condition, given early enough to matter before title passes. Late delivery has a cost. A buyer who gets the form only after making an offer can walk away within three days of receiving it by hand, or five days if it came by mail. Fill it out honestly and keep a copy with the date you delivered it.

Deeds, deeds of trust, releases and liens are all recorded by the Harrison County Chancery Clerk. The Biloxi recording office is at 730 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard. In Harrison, an archive county, the clerk's schedule charges $26.00 per deed, which covers indexing of the first five pages, and $1.00 for each page after that.

  • Gather the deed, any mortgage payoff statement and the current tax receipt.
  • Confirm that no code lien or open permit is attached to the property.
  • Let a Mississippi attorney or title company draft the deed. Charging to prepare a deed of conveyance counts as practicing law under Miss. Code Ann. 73-3-55.

sections.h2: When a cash offer makes sense
sections.html:
A cash route suits houses that need more work than a lender or retail buyer will take on, and sellers for whom speed counts for more than the last dollar. Cash Home Buyers prices Biloxi houses in their present shape. A sagging porch, a tired roof or leftover storm damage stays the buyer's job.

Common Biloxi situations include:

  • A house that sat through a storm season and still has deferred damage.
  • An inherited home where the heirs live elsewhere.
  • A rental with a tenant problem or a vacancy that drains money each month.
  • A move on a deadline.

Paying cash does not skip paperwork: a purchase contract, title search and recorded deed still apply. Weigh any offer against the net from a listed sale, once repair bills, agent fees and months of carrying costs are subtracted.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix storm damage before I sell my house in Biloxi?
faqs.a: No law requires repairs before a sale, but the city's permit and flood rules apply to any work you do. In a flood hazard area, repairs that reach 50 percent of the building's market value trigger new-construction standards, so call Community Development first.

faqs.q: When are Harrison County property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1 is the last day without interest. Statements go out December 1, interest of 0.5 percent a month begins February 2, and parcels still unpaid are sold on the last Monday of August.

faqs.q: Must I give a Mississippi buyer a disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Yes, if the sale is covered by Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523. Hand it over before title transfers, since a buyer who gets it late can back out for a few days.

faqs.q: Does homeowner's insurance cover flooding in Biloxi?
faqs.a: No. Flood damage needs a separate National Flood Insurance Program policy, and Biloxi's Community Rating System participation gives policyholders a premium discount.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Biloxi that is behind on taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, if the sale closes before the tax sale. Harrison County takes no real property payments once the sale begins, so the cutoff is 5:00 p.m. on the Friday before.
